title: SpinalExpect_Invasive
description: This dataset contains invasive spinal cord recordings from patients with neuropathic pain who underwent epidural electrode implantation in the cervical spinal canal. Subjects performed a temporal expectation task involving auditory cues and median nerve stimulation, with the primary objective of investigating whether temporal expectation modulates initial sensory processing at the spinal cord level. The study employed both fixed (1100 ms) and variable (100-2100 ms) cue-to-stimulus intervals across alternating experimental blocks.
methods_description: Eight patients with neuropathic pain following cervical epidural electrode implantation participated in the study. Recordings were obtained from eight epidural contacts (3 mm length, 1 mm spacing) placed alongside the dorsal cervical spinal cord, with the fourth contact serving as reference and an additional ground wire. Subjects received median nerve stimulation on the left wrist preceded by auditory cues at either fixed (1100 ms) or randomly varied (100-2100 ms) intervals. The task required subjects to count rare trials containing two rapid median nerve stimuli (80 ms interstimulus interval) within ~5 minute blocks.
